newsitem.title: GERMANY: Salamander sees 20 mln DMK loss in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Salamander sees 20 mln DMK loss in 1996.

text.p: German shoe maker Salamander AG said on Friday it expected a 20 million mark ($13 million) loss this year as a result of reorganization costs.
The company said it plans to write down 25 million marks to cover the cost of laying off workers and shifting production from Germany to low-wage countries, Salamander said in a statement.
The company did not say how many jobs would be eliminated.
Sales for 1996 are expected to hold steady at 1.3 bilion marks, and results should improve in 1997, the company said.

In 1995, the company reported net profit of 8.3 million marks on 1.34 billion in sales. Three costly joint ventures in Russia and Belarus dampened profits in 1996 and precipitated the departure of chief executive Gerhard Wacker.
Financial chief Claudius Hoasis was named earlier this month to succeed Wacker, who clashed with supervisory board chairman Franz Josef Dazert, the architect of the ventures.
